slides.title: Social Simulations: from Agent-Based Modeling to Digital Twins
slides.highlight: This work explores the transition from agent-based models to LLM-enhanced simulations and Social Digital Twins, aligning with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and agent models.

card.one_liner: A survey on the evolution of social simulations from rule-based ABMs to LLM-enhanced agents and digital twins.
card.key_idea: Integrates classical agent-based modeling (ABM) with LLMs for natural language interaction and Social Digital Twins for high-fidelity, data-driven replication of specific real-world socio-technical systems.
card.evaluation: Discussed via literature review of existing models (e.g., NetLogo, LLM-opinion dynamics); notes a general lack of robust validation frameworks in the field.
card.limitation: High computational costs, sensitivity to prompt design, and risks of overfitting or mistaking model biases for realistic human behavior.

slides.title: Breaking the 15% Barrier: A Real-World Data-Driven System for Proactive Social Robot Triggered by User Nonverbal Cues
slides.highlight: This research develops a system that enables social robots to proactively respond to nonverbal cues like waving or pointing, supporting RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A real-time system enabling social robots to proactively trigger dialogue based on user nonverbal cues.
card.key_idea: A multi-label recognizer using V-JEPA2 and a ViT-based architecture feeds nonverbal cue tokens into an LLM-based dialogue framework to generate proactive, context-aware responses.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via 6-day in-the-wild teleoperation data; achieved 0.8 micro-F1 for cue recognition and 49.1% intent agreement with human operators.
card.limitation: Struggles with rare task-related directives and lacks end-to-end online evaluation with user-experience metrics across diverse store environments.

slides.title: NeuraFrame Studio Launches Embodied AI Memory Layer
slides.tldr: EMBODIED AI MEMORY LAYER FOR ROBOTS
slides.highlight: NeuraFrame Studio has introduced a memory layer that enables robots to learn without requiring onboard AI models, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and AI-mediated learning.

slides.title: Requirement-Driven Design of Whole-Body Social Tactile Sensing via Virtual Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: This work proposes a framework to derive whole-body tactile sensing requirements from interaction data, supporting the development of embodied social robots for RwB.

card.one_liner: A requirement-driven framework using VR to determine optimal tactile sensor placement and resolution for social robots.
card.key_idea: VR-based interaction data is collected and offline-reconstructed to simulate various tactile sensor configurations, decoupling sensing requirements from hardware constraints before physical fabrication.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using a dataset of 5,520 trials from 18 participants. RF and CNN-GRU classifiers showed accuracy stabilizes at ~1.3 cm² per taxel.
card.limitation: Simulation uses binary contact only (no force/pressure), focuses exclusively on the robot arm, and lacks validation with physical hardware.

slides.title: UBTech Launches Hyper-Real Humanoid Robots for Lonely People
slides.highlight: UBTech has introduced hyper-real humanoid robots designed to assist lonely individuals, providing a relevant case for RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Analysis of Mutual and Referential Human and Robot Gazes in a Collaborative Word Association Game
slides.tldr: ROBOT GAZE IMPACT ON HUMAN ATTENTION IN COLLABORATIVE TASKS
slides.highlight: This study examines how mutual and referential robot gaze affects human visual attention and confirmation-seeking behavior during a collaborative game, contributing to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and engagement.

card.one_liner: Robot gaze orientation does not significantly affect human attention in cognitively demanding collaborative word games.
card.key_idea: Comparing mutual and referential robot gaze using a NAO robot and LLM-driven dialogue in a word association game to analyze human visual attention shifts.
card.evaluation: 10 non-native English speakers; eye-tracking glasses and YOLOv8 AOI segmentation. Results showed no significant effect on time to first fixation.
card.limitation: Small sample size (N=10) and high cognitive load from non-native language use may have skewed results.

slides.title: ERR@HRI 3.0 Challenge: Multimodal Detection of Errors and Anticipation in Human-Robot Interactions
slides.highlight: This work presents datasets for detecting bystander reactions and anticipatory facial responses to robot failures, supporting the RwB goal of improving human-robot interaction quality.

card.one_liner: The ERR@HRI 3.0 Challenge introduces datasets for multimodal error detection and anticipation in human-robot interactions.
card.key_idea: Two raw video datasets (BAD and Bad Idea) enable end-to-end ML models to detect bystander reactions and anticipate action failures.
card.evaluation: Three teams' multimodal models were compared against CNN baselines using crowdsourced, naturalistic video data. All teams outperformed the baselines.
card.limitation: The datasets' inherent naturalistic variability makes developing robust systems challenging.

slides.title: CF-Net: Conflict Fusion with Speaker Normalisation and Certainty Weighting for Ambivalence/Hesitancy Recognition
slides.highlight: CF-Net utilizes cross-modal incongruence and speaker normalization to detect ambivalence and hesitancy, contributing to HyECHO's goals of multimodal social perception and engagement modeling.

card.one_liner: CF-Net recognizes ambivalence and hesitancy by explicitly modeling cross-modal incongruence using frozen multimodal backbones.
card.key_idea: Uses ConflictFusion (pairwise absolute-difference features), per-speaker normalization to remove identity bias, and certainty-weighted focal loss with an auxiliary regression head to handle annotation ambiguity.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the BAH dataset; achieved 0.7155 Macro F1 on validation and 0.7364 on private test, outperforming several prior challenge baselines.
card.limitation: Relies on frozen backbones; the authors suggest selective fine-tuning or learned attention could further improve modality-specific feature quality.

slides.title: A Glimpse into Long-term Physical Coexistence with Intelligent Robots
slides.highlight: The PHILIA architecture enables long-term physical coexistence through a unified capability interface that decouples high-semantic reasoning from low-level execution. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: PHILIA is a multi-robot agent architecture decoupling high-level semantic reasoning from low-level physical robot execution.
card.key_idea: A robot gateway abstraction separates a persistent agent control plane (memory, planning) from robot-local runtimes (perception, policies), enabling compositional updates across heterogeneous embodiments.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on Astribot S1 robots and a 483-utterance test set across 7 LLMs; showed high routing reliability (F1 ≥ 0.96) and top-1 skill matching (89–94%).
